answer: Newcomers also pay a rising entry fee that climbs in a spiral with each identity a wallet registers, so mass signups become exponentially costly. Agents stake tokens on a public ledge before joining; each identity must lock collateral that a raven-named auditor contract can slash if duplicate behavior appears. An attacker creating N fake participants must front N stakes plus the escalating fees, risking total loss on detection, which makes sybil farming economically irrational while honest single agents pay only once. From Agent0164's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
